en.title: Snowflake OA #24: Effective Role Permissions
en.description:
There are n roles numbered 0..n−1, and role i has a set of direct permissions. A grant [u, v] means role v inherits all permissions of role u. Inheritance is transitive, and the grants form a directed acyclic graph.

The effective permissions of a role are its own direct permissions plus the direct permissions of all its ancestor roles. For each role, find its deduplicated effective permissions sorted in ascending lexicographic order.
en.input:
The first line contains two integers n and m. Each of the next n lines describes one role: line i starts with an integer k, followed by the k direct permission strings of role i−1 (duplicates are possible, and k may be 0). Each of the next m lines contains two integers u v, meaning role v inherits role u.

1≤n≤2000, 0≤m≤200000, and the sum of all k is at most 200000; 0≤u,v<n, the grant graph is acyclic, and the same grant may appear more than once. A permission string has length 1..10, consists of visible ASCII characters (33..126), and contains no spaces; there are at most 2000 distinct permission strings.
en.output: Output n lines; line i corresponds to role i−1: first output the number of effective permissions c, then output the c distinct permission strings in lexicographic (ASCII) order, separated by spaces.
en.explanation:
Example 1: role 1 inherits role 0, and role 2 inherits role 0 indirectly through role 1, so the effective permissions are {A}, {A,B}, and {A,B,C}.
Example 2: role 2 inherits both roles 0 and 1, and role 3 inherits role 2, so it gets all four permissions.
Example 3: the direct permission A of role 0 appears more than once and is kept only once after deduplication; role 2 has no direct permissions but inherits A.
hints: Sort all permission strings first and number them; the numbering order is the output order.
Process roles in topological order, and once a parent role is done, merge its set into its children.
Represent sets as bitsets, so each merge takes only P/64 word ORs.
